The story makes sophisticated use of metaphor throughout to explore themes of memory, emotional baggage, and the nature of relationships. 

Most notably, the recurring dream of the unvisited flat serves as an extended metaphor for the neglected, compartmentalized parts of Daniel’s own identity and past happiness—"a set of rooms he had paid for and never visited." When he finds the old keys, he further conceptualizes his past marriage as "the box marked *Didn't Work*," realizing he had locked away joyful parts of himself along with the failed relationship. 

Additionally, the writer uses smaller, original metaphors to capture the subtle emotional dynamics between Daniel and Isabel. The unspoken tension after he confesses his dream is described as "a third person who had come for lunch and not left," and their subsequent carefulness around each other takes on "the tone of two people carrying a ladder through a narrow house." Finally, the image of the canoe "going in a circle" serves as a concluding metaphor for the non-linear, imperfect way people navigate life and love.
